html:
Kati Thanda, or Lake Eyre, is a huge salt lake in the desert of northern South Australia, and at about 15 m below sea level the lowest point in Australia. Most years it is a dry crust of salt. It fills only when floods from Queensland run down the rivers of the Channel Country, such as Cooper Creek and the Diamantina, and it fills to the brim only a few times a century. Its basin covers about a sixth of the continent.

Aboriginal peoples have lived around it and its rivers for tens of thousands of years: the Arabana to the west and south, the Dieri and Dhirari to the east where Cooper Creek comes in, and upstream in Queensland the Pitta Pitta, Guwa and Iningai. Trade routes along the rivers carried pituri, ochre and grindstones.

Its English name is for the explorer Edward John Eyre, who saw it in 1840. In 2012 the courts recognised Arabana native title over the lake, and the name Kati Thanda was added.
